thread:
incident-bot: Paging SRE oncall — automated alert: api-gateway error rate spike detected in edge cluster us-east-1. 502/504s elevated across multiple frontends. start=2026-03-15T12:03:41Z, error_rate=18% (baseline 0.4%), traffic=~1.2k rps, p95 latency=4.2s. Pager sent to @sre-oncall :rotating_light:

sre-oncall: Oncall here, taking lead. Thanks bot. Setting channel to incident-mode. @michelle you available to help with telemetry?

michelle: I'm in. Pulling SLO dashboards now — looks like spike started ~12:02 UTC and ramped quickly. Edge 502s correlate with backend 502s from svc-auth and svc-payments.

mike: I see similar from synthetic probes (edge/health-check) returning 502s intermittently. Stack traces show "upstream reset" in gateway logs. Posting tail of gateway logs for last 90s:
```
[12:03:15] edge-proxy-1 upstream reset for connid=34212 svc-payments 502
[12:03:18] edge-proxy-3 upstream timeout id=9876 svc-auth 504
[12:03:22] edge-proxy-2 connection refused to 10.2.18.45:443 (svc-payments)
```

anya: Not seeing deploys in last 30m for edge, but there was a config rollout 17m ago: "edge-ingress: upstream-retry-policy" changed from 3->1. Could that increase visible 502s?

mike: Hmm, decreased retries usually reduces client-visible 502s (fewer retries), but should not spike backend resets. Also seeing larger TCP retransmits on egress LB.

infra-bot: Noted: ASG_autoscale_event at 11:58 UTC for gateway-nodes-us-east triggered scale-down (desired -> 6 nodes). Current gateway pool size: 6.

sre-oncall: Okay, two potential correlated events: autoscale scale-down ~12:00 (less headroom) + config change ~11:48 (retry policy). Let's get quick checklist: 1) freeze config rollouts 2) scale gateway up 3) enable regional fallback for critical routes 4) reduce fanout to unstable upstreams.

michelle: Freezing config rollouts now — disabling auto-rollout for ingress config in console.

mike: Scaling gateway ASG to 12 now (fast scale). Command: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name gw-us-east --desired-capacity 12` 

infra-bot: Scale request accepted. New instances pending.

support-lead: Support stack: we have ~45 open customer tickets mentioning 502s in last 8 minutes, highest concentration in EU and US east. Notable: large merchant A reporting failed checkout webhooks. Tagging product-ops.

product-ops: Aware. We need customer impact summary ASAP for comms. Can someone confirm which downstream services are failing most?

michelle: From traces: svc-payments ~62% of failed requests, svc-auth ~22%, everything else ~16%. Root cause looks upstream of gateway or at upstream capacity.

mike: While nodes scale, let's reduce gateway fanout to svc-payments by routing a subset to payment-standby cluster. Executing traffic-shift for /payments/* -> payments-standby (10%). Command run: `rdwctl routing shift payments 10 --from payments-main --to payments-standby`

sre-oncall: Also enable temporary circuit breaker on gateway for payment endpoints to fail-fast on upstream 5xx to avoid head-of-line blocking. Applying policy now.

anya: Rolling out circuit breaker policy to edge: `curl -XPOST https://console.internal/api/v1/edge/policies -d '{"route":"/payments","cb":"fast-fail","threshold":0.2}'` (applied).

mike: New gateway nodes are joining. Health checks passing for new instances. Error% dropped to ~9% after partial traffic shift and scaling. p95 down to 1.8s.

incident-bot: Update: autoscale complete, gw-us-east desired=12, in-service=12.

michelle: I dug into payment cluster's pods — some backends are returning 502 due to a recent kernel upgrade on that fleet (kube-drain ops performed earlier). There are connection backlog limits hitting. Logs from payments-main pods:
```
[12:01:57] http: accept tcp 10.2.18.45:443: accept4: too many open files
[12:02:05] runtime error: accept: connection refused
```

mike: That explains connection refused. Rolling restart of effected payment pod group (kube rollout restart deploy/payments-main -n payments) in progress.

anya: While rolling restart goes, lowering gateway upstream connections timeout threshold to shed slow connections: `edge.conf set upstream_timeout=2s` then reload edge.

sre-oncall: Confirmed reload applied. Also reduced retry budget to 0 for /payments route to avoid retry storms.

support-lead: Triage note for customers: increased 5xx on checkouts and webhooks between 12:02-12:18 UTC; mitigation in progress. ETA to customers: 30m for broader restoration, we'll follow up with post-incident summary.

product-ops: Drafting status update. Key facts: 1) Root cause: connection exhaustion on payments fleet coincident with gateway scale-down; 2) Impact: intermittent 502/504 for checkout/webhook flows; 3) Mitigation: scaled gateway, traffic-shift to standby, circuit breaker, restart of payments pods, lowered upstream timeouts.

mike: Payments deployment restarted, pods passing readiness. Errors continuing but trending down. Error rate now 3.7%.

michelle: I can confirm traces now show successful end-to-end requests for previously failing transactions. Sending sample:
```json
{"trace_id":"abc123","route":"/payments/charge","status":200,"latency_ms":380}
```

sre-oncall: Good work. Next steps: 1) monitor for 30m, 2) keep circuit breaker and routing changes for 15m stable window, 3) open incident ticket (INC-\n) and assign to infra + payments oncall for root cause RCA (kernel upgrade coordination + connection limits).

infra-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-20260315-0917 (internal link: https://tickets.internal/INC-20260315-0917). Assigned: infra-team, payments-team.

support-lead: Notifying top 20 affected customers with initial incident note and will post to status.redwood.ai.

product-ops: I'll prepare a postmortem template. We should include timeline, contributing factors (ASG scale-down window, kernel changes on payments fleet, config retry policy), and suggested mitigations (connection limit tuning, decouple kernel updates from high-traffic windows, improve autoscaler aggressiveness).

mike: Quick follow-up check: run `ss -s` on payments nodes shows tcp backlog drops after restart; CPU and mem stable.

michelle: Observability tasks: create an alert for sudden spike in accept4 errors and a synthetic test that exercises /payments/charge in addition to generic health-checks.

sre-oncall: Marking incident as under control. Keeping channel open for 30m monitoring. If error rate creeps above 5% we re-escalate. Thanks everyone. :heart:

support-lead: ETA for next update to customers in 20m.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to: mitigating -> under_control at 12:12:01Z, severity downgraded.

sre-oncall: Leaving a note for RCA: check autoscaler cooldown threshold, node draining schedule, and recent kernel patch runbook. Assigning toiya? (assigning in ticket).

anya: Adding logs and timestamped config diffs to ticket. Will follow with root cause doc.

michelle: Will take on the monitoring action items.

product-ops: Closing comms loop once support posts status update.

sre-oncall: Closing handoff. If anyone sees a regression ping here or escalate to pager. Good job team.
